articles.title: A New Summer Morning
articles.text:
Summer vacation is here! Yesterday was the last day of school, and today is the first day of my long vacation. I don't need to get up at six anymore, but I still get up early. Why? Because my mom has a rule: in our house, everyone gets up before eight, even in summer.
This morning, I got up at seven thirty. I brushed my teeth, washed my face, and ate breakfast with my family. We had eggs, toast, and milk. Dad said, "Don't be lazy this summer. Early birds have more time to play!" I think he is right. When I get up early, the morning feels long and cool, and I can finish my homework before lunch. Then I have the whole afternoon to play. What a great start to summer!

questions.q: What is the rule in the writer's house?
What did the writer have for breakfast?
Why does the writer like getting up early?
options: The morning feels long and cool, and there is more time to play.
Because Dad gives money to early birds.
questions.answer: The morning feels long and cool, and there is more time to play.

articles.title: My Favorite Room
articles.text:
My home is not big, but I love every room in it. The living room has a soft sofa and a big window. The kitchen always smells good because Mom loves cooking. But my favorite room is my bedroom.
My bedroom is small. There is a bed, a desk, and a bookshelf. Last month, my room was very messy. There were books on the floor and clothes on the chair. I couldn't find my favorite comic book! So I made a change. Now I clean my room every Sunday. I put my books on the shelf and my clothes in the closet.
A clean room feels comfortable. Now I like to read and draw in my bedroom. It is small, but it is the best place in the world to me.

questions.q: Which room is the writer's favorite?
Why couldn't the writer find the comic book last month?
options: It was in the living room.
Mom put it in the closet.

questions.q: How often does the writer clean the room now?

articles.title: Helping at Home
articles.text:
During summer vacation, everyone in my family has a job at home. Mom cooks the meals. Dad washes the dishes after dinner. My little sister feeds the cat and waters the plants. And me? I sweep the floor and take out the trash.
At first, I didn't like my jobs. Sweeping the floor is boring, and the trash is smelly! But then Mom told me, "When we all help a little, nobody has to work a lot." Now I understand. Mom is busy, and our help makes her smile.
Last night, we finished the housework in twenty minutes because everyone helped. After that, we ate watermelon and watched a movie together in the living room. Helping at home is not so bad. It makes our family time longer and happier.

questions.q: What are the writer's jobs at home?
options: Sweeping the floor and taking out the trash.
Feeding the cat and watering plants.
Cleaning the bathroom and washing clothes.
questions.answer: Sweeping the floor and taking out the trash.

questions.q: Who washes the dishes after dinner?
Why did the family finish the housework in twenty minutes last night?
options: Because the house was already clean.

articles.title: A Big Family Dinner
articles.text:
Last Saturday, we had a big family dinner at my grandparents' house. My aunt, my uncle, and my three cousins all came. There were twelve people in the house!
Grandma cooked all afternoon. She made chicken soup, fish, and fried noodles. My aunt brought her famous dumplings. Everyone says her dumplings are the best in the family. My cousins and I set the table and helped carry the dishes.
At dinner, the adults chatted about work and the summer weather. We kids talked about our vacation plans. My cousin Kevin wants to learn swimming. I told him about my plan to read ten books this summer. He laughed and said, "Ten books? You can do it!"
After dinner, we ate mango ice together. I love big family dinners. The food is great, but being together is even better.

questions.q: Where was the big family dinner?
Who made the famous dumplings?
What is the writer's plan for the summer?

articles.title: Busy Dad, Free Dad
articles.text:
My dad is a very busy man. On weekdays, he gets up at six, drives to work, and comes home after seven in the evening. Sometimes he still answers phone calls at night. I often see him yawn at dinner.
But on the weekend, Dad becomes a different person. He is free! On Saturday mornings, he sleeps until nine. Then he makes a big brunch for us. In the afternoon, he plays basketball with me in the park, and we always buy a cold drink after the game.
Last night I asked him, "Dad, are you tired of your busy life?" He smiled and said, "I work hard on weekdays, so I can enjoy my free time with you on weekends. That's my favorite habit." I hope I can be like Dad — work hard, play hard, and always have time for family.

questions.q: What time does Dad get up on weekdays?
What does Dad do with the writer on Saturday afternoons?
options: He plays basketball in the park.
questions.answer: He plays basketball in the park.

questions.q: What does Dad think about his busy life?
options: Working hard on weekdays lets him enjoy free time with family on weekends.
He wants to change his job soon.
He is too tired to play with his son.
questions.answer: Working hard on weekdays lets him enjoy free time with family on weekends.

articles.title: A Good Night's Sleep
articles.text:
Do you sleep well at night? Last week, I didn't. Every night, I played games on my phone in bed. I told myself, "Just ten more minutes." But the ten minutes always became one hour! I went to sleep after midnight and got up at noon. I felt tired all day, and my eyes hurt.
Mom saw the problem. She made a new rule: no phones in the bedroom after ten. At first, I thought the rule was terrible. But something interesting happened. Without my phone, I took a warm shower, read a book, and fell asleep quickly. I slept for nine hours and had a sweet dream.
Now I feel fresh in the morning. My eyes don't hurt anymore. Good sleep is like a superpower — it makes everything better. Maybe Mom's rules are not so bad after all.

questions.q: Why did the writer sleep badly last week?
options: The writer played phone games in bed until after midnight.
The writer drank too much tea.
questions.answer: The writer played phone games in bed until after midnight.

questions.q: What is Mom's new rule?
options: No phones in the bedroom after ten.
questions.answer: No phones in the bedroom after ten.

questions.q: How does the writer feel now?

articles.title: Sunday, Our Family Day
articles.text:
In my family, Sunday is "Family Day." It is our weekly habit. We don't make other plans on Sunday. We just spend the day together.
This morning, we got up late and made pancakes together. Dad flipped the pancakes high in the air, and one almost hit the ceiling! We laughed so hard. After breakfast, we cleaned the house together. With four people working, it took only thirty minutes.
In the afternoon, we walked to the park near our home. Mom and Dad chatted under a big tree. My sister and I shared an ice cream and fed the fish in the pond. Before dinner, we called Grandma and chatted with her for an hour.
My classmates say Family Day sounds boring. I don't think so. A simple day together makes everyone happy. It is the warmest part of my week.

questions.q: What is Sunday in the writer's family?
What happened when Dad flipped the pancakes?
What did the writer and the sister do in the park?
options: They shared an ice cream and fed the fish.
They rode bikes around the pond.
They slept under a big tree.
questions.answer: They shared an ice cream and fed the fish.
